frames.title: SubInvoker.Apply
frames.explanation: Every step whose anchor cannot be found must still render its lines, its callout and its links — only the pulse is dropped. Each failing case sits BESIDE a case where the same mechanism succeeds, so a step that draws nothing cannot be mistaken for an instrument that is simply blind.

relations.note: a resolvable pair, so the link drawing is a control for the token drops below

steps.note: Read this step first. If it does not pulse, every drop below is meaningless.
steps.ttsText: The guarded value is the anchor here, and it is present, so this step pulses.

steps.note: The plain miss. Lines, callout and links must all still draw.
steps.ttsText: This step names an identifier that does not appear anywhere in the method, which is the simplest way an anchor fails.

steps.note: `running` is on all three of these lines. `Running` is on none — the match is case-sensitive, and this is the pair that proves it.
steps.ttsText: Capitalising the first letter is enough to miss: the anchor is matched exactly, not loosely.

steps.explanation: In the file, outside the range
steps.note: `running` occurs four times in this method but not once in lines 82–84. The search window is the STEP's ranges, never the whole file.
steps.ttsText: The running total is named plenty of times in this method, but not in the lines this step is about, so there is nothing here to mark.

steps.explanation: CONTROL — resolves only on the second pass
steps.note: A non-identifier anchor: the whole-word pass rejects `Apply(` because a letter follows the bracket's left flank, and the bare-substring pass is what finds it. This is the pair that justifies `resolveToken` running twice.
steps.ttsText: An anchor that includes its opening bracket cannot match as a whole word, and is found by the substring pass instead.

steps.note: Dropped before the search runs at all — the upstream guard, not a failed match.
steps.ttsText: An anchor that is nothing but whitespace is discarded before anything is looked for.

steps.explanation: CONTROL — the last word is that it still works
steps.note: Ending on a hit rather than a miss, so a run that silently stopped pulsing partway through is visible.
steps.ttsText: The guard call resolves normally, which closes the plan on a case that works.
